article.heading: Concurrence of inadmissibility and admissibility of cooperation

content.p: If the act of which the defendant is accused constitutes an offence under two or more provisions of Swiss criminal law, the request may be granted only in respect of those offences for which there are no reasons for inadmissibility and if there is a guarantee that the requesting State will respect the conditions imposed.

Cooperation shall not be permitted if the proceedings concern an act that constitutes an offence under two or more provisions of Swiss or foreign criminal law and if, with regard to one of these offences, which covers the act in all its aspects, a request may not be granted.

No Swiss national may, without his written consent, be extradited or surrendered to a foreign State for prosecution or for the execution of a sentence. Consent may be withdrawn up to the time when the surrender is ordered.
Paragraph 1 does not apply to transit or return of a Swiss national who is temporarily surrendered by a third State to the Swiss authorities.

chapter.heading: Personal Data, File and Process Management System

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOJ shall run a personal data, file and process management system that may contain sensitive personal data obtained through forms of cooperation governed by this Act. This data may be processed in order to:

item.p: identify whether data on a particular person is being processed;
process data on processes;
organise work procedures rationally and efficiently;
conduct a process check;
compile statistics.

blockList.listIntroduction: In order to comply with the processing purposes mentioned in paragraph 1, the system shall contain:

item.p: personal details of persons on whom data is being processed;
data necessary for the localisation and proper administration of the dossier;
documents on electronically stored processes and entries.

content.p:
The Federal Office of Police and the State Secretariat for Migration

If the Federal Office of Police carries out the tasks of the FOJ under this Act, it shall also have online access to the data defined in paragraph 2 letter b.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council shall specify the details, and in particular:

item.p: in the case of the recording of data in accordance with paragraph 2 letters a and b, data on the judicial authorities involved in the mutual assistance proceedings and data on the offences giving rise to the request for mutual assistance;
the period of time that the data is kept and the archiving of the data;
the agencies of the FOJ that are authorised to process the data directly in the system and the data that in individual cases may be disclosed to other authorities.

chapter.heading: Protection of Personal Data

article.heading: Right to information in pending proceedings

blockList.listIntroduction: Where mutual assistance proceedings are pending, the person who is the object of a request for international cooperation in criminal matters shall be allowed access to the personal data related to them and the following information:

item.p: the purpose of and legal basis for the data processing;
the period that the personal data will be retained or, if this is not possible, the criteria for determining this period;
the recipients or the categories of recipients;
the available information on the origin of the personal data;
the information that they require to be able to assert their rights.

blockList.listIntroduction: The competent authority may refuse to provide the information, limit the information provided or defer provision of the information if there are grounds for doing so under Article 80b paragraph 2 or if:

item.p: it is necessary because of overriding interests of third parties;
it is necessary because of overriding public interests, in particular relating to the internal or external security of Switzerland; or
an enquiry, an investigation, court proceedings or international cooperation proceedings in criminal matters may be prejudiced by providing the person concerned with information.

article.heading: Restriction of the right to information in relation to requests for arrest for the purpose of extradition

content.p: Any person may request information on whether Switzerland has received a request from a foreign state to make an arrest for the purpose of extradition. This right may be asserted at the FOJ. If the request is made to a different authority, that authority shall forward the request immediately to the FOJ.

If a person requests information on whether the FOJ has received a request to make an arrest for the purpose of extradition, the FOJ shall notify the person that no data about them has been unlawfully processed and that the person can request the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (the FDPIC) to enquire as to whether any data on them has been lawfully processed.
Amended by Annex 1 No II 29 of the Data Protection Act of 25 Sept. 2020, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 491; BBl 2017 6941).

The FDPIC shall conduct the enquiries; he shall notify the person concerned either that no data about them has been unlawfully processed or that he has opened an investigation under Article 49 of the Data Protection Act of 25 September 2020
SR 235.1 in the case of errors in the processing of personal data.
Amended by Annex 1 No II 29 of the Data Protection Act of 25 Sept. 2020, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 491; BBl 2017 6941).

If the FDPIC identifies errors in the data processing, he shall order the FOJ to rectify the same.
Amended by Annex 1 No II 29 of the Data Protection Act of 25 Sept. 2020, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 491; BBl 2017 6941).
The notifications under paragraphs 2 and 3 shall always be worded in the same way and shall not mention the grounds.
The notification under paragraph 3 may not be contested.
In derogation from paragraph 2, the FOJ is entitled to provide the person concerned with the requested information if the requesting state gives its advance consent.

article.heading: Right to have personal data corrected or deleted

content.p: The person who is the object of a request for international cooperation in criminal matters may request that the competent authority correct or delete the personal data relating to them that is being processed in contravention of this Act.

blockList.listIntroduction: Instead of deleting the personal data, the competent authority shall restrict the processing if:

item.p: the data subject disputes the accuracy of the personal data but it cannot be established whether the data is correct or incorrect;
overriding interests, in particular those set out in Article 80b paragraph 2, so require; or
deletion may prejudice proceedings on international cooperation in criminal matters or foreign proceedings giving rise to the request for cooperation in criminal matters.

content.p: The competent authority shall immediately notify the authority that has transmitted, made available or disclosed the personal data about the measures taken in accordance with paragraph 1 or 2.

The relevant foreign authority is responsible for checking the accuracy of personal data that has been obtained as evidence or personal data relating to criminal offences giving rise to the request for international cooperation in criminal matters.

The data protection rules that apply to the disclosure of personal data to the competent authorities of States that are linked with Switzerland through one of the Schengen association agreements (the Schengen States) must not be stricter than the rules that apply to the disclosure of personal data to Swiss law enforcement authorities.

Specific legislation that provides for stricter data protection rules for the disclosure of personal data to the competent foreign authorities does not apply to disclosure to the competent authorities of the Schengen States.

article.heading: Disclosure of personal data to a third country or an international body

content.p: Personal data may not be disclosed to the competent authority of a State that is not linked with Switzerland through one of the Schengen association agreements (a third country) or to an international body if, as a result, the privacy of the data subject would be seriously jeopardised, in particular because of the lack of adequate protection.

blockList.listIntroduction: Adequate protection is guaranteed by:

item.p: the legislation of the third country, provided the European Union has confirmed this in a decision;
an international agreement;
specific guarantees.

blockList.listIntroduction: In derogation from paragraph 1, personal data may be disclosed to the competent authority of a third country or to an international body if disclosure is necessary in the case in question:

item.p: to protect the life or physical integrity of the data subject or a third party;
to prevent an imminent and serious threat to the public security of a Schengen State or of a third country;
to prevent, detect or prosecute a criminal offence or to execute a criminal judgment, unless overriding legitimate interests of the data subject preclude disclosure;

to exercise or enforce legal rights against an authority competent to prevent, detect or prosecute a criminal offence or to execute a criminal judgment, unless overriding legitimate interests of the data subject preclude disclosure.

article.heading: Disclosure of personal data by a Schengen State to a third country or an international body

blockList.listIntroduction: Personal data that are transmitted or made available by a Schengen State may be disclosed to the competent authority of a third country or to an international body if:

item.p: disclosure is required to prevent, detect or prosecute a criminal offence or to execute a criminal judgment;
the Schengen State that transmitted or made available the personal data has given prior consent to disclosure; and
the requirements of Article 11f are met.

blockList.listIntroduction: In derogation from paragraph 1 letter b, personal data may be disclosed in an individual case if:

item.p: the prior consent of the Schengen State cannot be obtained in time; and
disclosure is necessary to prevent an imminent and serious threat to the public security of a Schengen State or of a third country or to protect the essential interests of a Schengen State.

content.p: The Schengen State shall be notified immediately of any disclosure under paragraph 2.

article.heading: Procedure for the disclosure of personal data

content.p: The competent authority shall notify the recipient about the reliability of the personal data disclosed and of the extent to which they are up to date.

blockList.listIntroduction: It shall also disclose any additional information to the recipient that may as far as possible be used to distinguish:

item.p: between the various categories of data subjects;
between personal data based on facts and personal data based on personal assessments.

content.p: The obligation to notify the recipient does not apply if the information mentioned in paragraphs 1 and 2 is evident from the personal data themselves or from the circumstances.

Unless this Act specifies otherwise, the federal administrative authorities shall apply, by analogy, the Federal Act of 20 December 1968
SR 172.021 on Administrative Procedure, and the cantonal authorities their own procedural rules. Procedural acts are governed by the procedural law in criminal matters.

The cantonal and federal provisions on the suspension of time limits do not apply.

article.heading:
Suspension of limitation periods
The suspension of the effects of the time limitation provisions has been abolished by Art. 97 ff. of the Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) and time limits for execution have been replaced by an extension of the regular time limit (AS 2006 3459; BBl 1999 1979).. Filing a criminal complaint

blockList.listIntroduction: In proceedings under this Act, the following shall be considered to have effect in Switzerland:

item.p: the suspension of a limitation period under the law of the requesting State;
the filing of a criminal complaint with a foreign authority within the time limit provided for if this is so required under Swiss law.

content.p: If a criminal complaint is required only under Swiss law, no sentence may be imposed or executed in Switzerland if the victim makes objections.

article.heading: Taking account of the period in detention

content.p:
Article 69 of the Swiss Criminal Code
SR 311.0. See now art. 51. applies when taking account of the period spent on remand or in detention abroad due to proceedings under this Act.

Articles 429 and 431 CrimPC

Amended by Annex 1 No II 13 of the Criminal Procedure Code of 5 Oct. 2007, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2010 1881; BBl 2006 1085).
The Confederation shall pay the compensation if a federal authority makes or executes a request. It may require reimbursement from the canton that caused the request to be made.

The compensation may be reduced or refused if the defendant has provoked the investigation or the detention through his fault, or has, without reason, obstructed or delayed the proceedings.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: Compensation for detention pending extradition served in Switzerland may also be reduced or refused if the requesting State:

item.p: withdraws the request for search and arrest with a view to extradition; or

does not present the request for extradition with the necessary enclosures within the deadline set.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p:
The likelihood of the injured party being able to obtain damages in the foreign State must be taken into account when the decision is made to reduce or refuse the compensation.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

The cantons shall participate in the conduct of extradition proceedings. Unless federal law provides otherwise, they are required to execute the requests for other forms of mutual assistance and the transfer of proceedings and to execute criminal judgments. The cantons shall be subject to the supervision of the Confederation provided this Act applies.

The FOJ shall receive the requests from abroad and file Swiss requests. It shall handle extradition requests and arrange for requests for other assistance, transfer of proceedings and execution of criminal judgments to be examined by the appropriate cantonal or federal authorities if their execution is not obviously inadmissible.

blockList.listIntroduction: It shall decide:

item.p: whether to require a guarantee of reciprocity (Art. 8 para. 1);
on the appropriate procedure (Art. 19);
on the admissibility of Swiss requests (Art. 30, para. 1).

content.p: It may transfer the conduct of proceedings wholly or partly to the federal authority which would be competent to prosecute the offence if it had been committed in Switzerland.

It may also decide on the admissibility of assistance and allow its execution in accordance with Article 79 letter a.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: The competent authority shall execute requests promptly. It shall decide without delay.

It shall on request provide the FOJ with information on the status of the proceedings, the reasons for any delay and the measures being considered. If the delay is not justified, the FOJ may take the matter up with the appropriate supervisory authority.
When the competent authority, without reason, refuses to or delays in issuing a ruling, its conduct shall be regarded as equivalent to a negative decision subject to appeal.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: At the express request of another State, provisional measures may be taken by the competent authority to preserve the existing situation, to safeguard threatened legal interests or to protect jeopardised evidence unless the proceedings under this Act clearly appear to be inadmissible or inappropriate.

If any delay would jeopardise the proceedings and if there is sufficient information to determine whether all the conditions are met, the FOJ may likewise order provisional measures as soon as a request is announced. Such measures shall be revoked if the foreign State does not make the request within the deadline set.
Appeals filed against rulings based on this Article do not have suspensive effect.

article.heading: Surveillance of postal and telecommunications traffic

content.p: In extradition cases, the FOJ may, at the express request of another State order the surveillance of postal and telecommunications traffic in order to establish the whereabouts of the defendant.

blockList.listIntroduction: In other mutual assistance cases, the following authorities may order the surveillance of postal and telecommunications traffic:

item.p: the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland or of the Cantonal Public Prosecutor;
the FOJ, if it is executing the request for mutual assistance itself.

blockList.listIntroduction: The surveillance order must be submitted to the following authorities for approval:

item.p: by the federal authorities: the federal compulsory measures court;
by the cantonal authorities: the cantonal compulsory measures court.

content.p:
The requirements for surveillance and the procedure shall otherwise be governed by Articles 269–279 CrimPC
SR 312.0 and the Federal Act of 6 October 2000
[AS 2001 3096; 2003 2133 annex No 18, 3043 No I 2; 2004 2149, 3693; 2006 2197 annex No 84, 5437 Art. 2 No 3; 2007 921 annex No 3, 5437 annex No II 7; 2010 1881 annex 1 No II 26, 3267 annex II 14; 2012 3745 annex No 7; 2017 4095 annex No II 12. AS 2018 117]. See now the FA of 18 March 2016 (SR 780.1). on the Surveillance of Postal and Telecommunications Traffic.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Art. 2 No 2 of the FD of 18 March 2011 (Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime), in force since 1 Jan. 2012 (AS 2011 6293; BBl 2010 4697).

blockList.listIntroduction: The federal or cantonal authority dealing with a request for mutual assistance may order the transmission of electronic communications traffic data to another State before conclusion of the mutual assistance proceedings if:

item.p: provisional measures indicate that the communication that is the subject of the request originated abroad; or

the data was acquired by the executing authority based on an order for authorised real-time surveillance (Art. 269–281 CrimPC
SR 312.0).

content.p: The data may not be used in evidence before the ruling on granting and the extent of mutual assistance is legally binding.
Notice of the ruling under paragraph 1 and any order or authorisation for surveillance must be given to the FOJ immediately.

If the defendant is abroad and if, according to the laws of the State to which the request is to be made, there is a choice between different procedures, preference shall be given to the procedure which appears to ensure the better social rehabilitation.

article.heading: Suspension of criminal proceedings or of the execution of a penalty

blockList.listIntroduction: At the request of the FOJ, the competent authority may temporarily suspend criminal proceedings or the execution of a sentence against a defendant abroad for another offence if:

item.p: the sentence imposed in Switzerland is not of great importance in comparison to the one likely to be imposed abroad; or
execution of the sentence in Switzerland does not seem appropriate.

content.p: On conclusion of the criminal proceedings abroad, the Swiss authority shall decide whether or not to resume the suspended proceedings or the execution of the penalty.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: In the interest of proceedings carried out in another State and permitted under this Act, the FOJ may permit transit through Swiss territory and approve the measures required therefor on submission of a request by the State concerned or a third State without hearing the person concerned. There is no right of appeal against the decision and ancillary measures. They shall be notified only to the requesting State.

blockList.listIntroduction: No approval shall be required if the detained person is to be transported by aircraft over Swiss territory without a stopover landing. In the event of an unscheduled stopover landing, the detained person may be kept in custody only if:

item.p: the requirements for his arrest under Article 44 are met; or
the State arranging for the transport to be made has previously informed the FOJ by indicating the reason for surrender and the offence which is the basis for it.

content.p: Only the FOJ may interrupt the transit to prosecute an offence or to execute a criminal judgment in Switzerland.

The defendant may appoint a legal adviser. If he chooses not to do so or is not in a position to do so, a legal adviser shall be officially appointed if required to safeguard the interests of the defendant.

Other persons who are affected by the mutual assistance measures or who, as injured parties, are present at enquiries, may, if the safeguarding of their interests so requires, be assisted by a legal adviser while mutual assistance measures are being carried out and, provided the object of the investigation is not prejudiced, be represented by him.

Persons who are the subject of foreign criminal proceedings may challenge rulings only if they are personally and directly affected by a mutual assistance measure and if they have an interest worthy of legal protection in the measure being revoked or changed.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

item.p: granting extradition; or

authorising the transmission abroad of classified information or the handing over of objects or assets.

content.p: Rulings and decisions issued by federal and cantonal authorities must give notice of the possible appellate remedies, the appellate authority and the deadline for filing an appeal.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by Annex No 30 of the FA of 17 June 2005 on the Federal Administrative Court, with effect from 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).
Repealed by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, with effect from 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

article.heading:
Appeal
Amended by Annex No 30 of the FA of 17 June 2005 on the Federal Administrative Court, in force since 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).

content.p:
First instance rulings by cantonal and federal authorities are subject to an appeal directly to the Appeals Chamber of the Federal Criminal Court unless this Act stipulates otherwise.
Amended by Annex No 30 of the FA of 17 June 2005 on the Federal Administrative Court, in force since 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).

An appeal against a Swiss request to another State is only admissible if that State is requested to assume responsibility for the criminal proceedings or the execution of a criminal judgment. In this case, only defendants who are habitually resident in Switzerland are entitled to appeal.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

An appeal against a Swiss request for transferring responsibility for the execution of a criminal judgment in connection with a transfer under Article 101 paragraph 2 is admissible.
Inserted by Art. 2 of the FD of 19 Dec. 2003, in force since 1 Oct. 2004 (AS 2004 4161 4162; BBl 2002 4340)

The FOJ may appeal against rulings by cantonal authorities as well as against decisions by the Federal Criminal Court. The cantonal authority is entitled to appeal against the decision of the FOJ not to make a request.
Amended by Annex No 30 of the FA of 17 June 2005 on the Federal Administrative Court, in force since 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).
An appeal may also be filed against the inadmissible or obviously improper application of foreign law.

…
Repealed by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, with effect from 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

The Appeals Chamber of the Federal Criminal Court is not bound by the applications made by the parties.
Amended by Annex No 30 of the FA of 17 June 2005 on the Federal Administrative Court, in force since 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p:
Rulings made by the Department under Article 17 paragraph 1 shall be subject to appeal to the Federal Council. …
Sentence repealed by Annex No 30 of the FA of 17 June 2005 on the Federal Administrative Court, with effect from 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).

Articles 27 to 31 apply to all procedures under this Act subject to the special rules of procedure provided for in the other parts of this Act.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).
Foreign requests shall be addressed directly to the FOJ.
Requests which are addressed to an inappropriate authority shall be forwarded ex officio. The requesting authority shall be duly notified.
Requests in connection with an arrest shall be dealt with without delay.
The non-acceptance or refusal of a request must be substantiated.
Requests shall be made in writing.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following information must be provided in a request:

item.p: the office issuing the request and, if applicable, the authority having criminal jurisdiction;
the subject matter of and the reason for the request;
the legal term for the offence;
details that are as exact and complete as possible on the person who is the subject of the criminal proceedings.

blockList.listIntroduction: To permit the legal assessment of the offence, the following shall be added:

item.p: a summary of the relevant allegations, except in the case of requests for service;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).
item.p: the wording of the regulations applicable at the place where the offence was committed, except for requests for assistance in accordance with Part Three of this Act.

content.p: Foreign official records need not be legalised.
Foreign requests and their enclosures shall be submitted in German, French or Italian or be accompanied by a translation into one of these languages. Translations must be officially certified.
If a request does not meet the formal requirements, its correction or completion may be demanded; the ordering of provisional measures is not affected thereby.
The FOJ may receive requests directly from the ministry of justice of the requesting State.

When provisional measures must be taken or in urgent cases, the intervention of the International Criminal Police organisation (ICPO Interpol) may be enlisted or a copy of the written request may be sent directly to the authority competent for its execution.
Swiss authorities may not address to another State requests which they themselves could not grant under this Act.

The FOJ is competent for requests for extradition, transfer of proceedings or execution of criminal judgments; it shall take action at the request of the requesting Swiss authority.
Amended by Annex 1 No 11 of the FA of 17 June 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 468; BBl 2019 6697).
Conditions which the requested State attaches to the execution of the request must be observed by the Swiss authorities.
The FOJ may decline to make a request if the importance of the offence does not justify the proceedings.

The FOJ shall inform the requesting Swiss authority immediately if the requested State requires a court order for a requested mutual assistance measure.
Inserted by Annex 1 No 11 of the FA of 17 June 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 468; BBl 2019 6697).
As a rule, foreign requests shall be executed free of charge.
The Federal Council shall determine the conditions under which the requesting State may be charged full or partial costs.
The costs of a Swiss request that are reimbursed to another State shall be charged to the proceedings that caused the request to be made.
The Federal Council shall regulate the sharing of costs between the Confederation and the cantons.

Foreign nationals may be surrendered to another State for prosecution or enforcement of a sentence involving deprivation of liberty for acts which come under its criminal jurisdiction if that State requests extradition or if it accepts the Swiss request to prosecute the offence or enforce the judgment.

Children and juveniles as defined in the Swiss Criminal Code
SR 311.0 whose extradition is requested shall, if possible, be repatriated by the juvenile authorities. The same applies to persons between the ages of 18 and 20 if extradition could endanger their mental development or social rehabilitation.
Repatriation shall have the effects of an extradition.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, with effect from 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: Extradition is permitted if, according to the documents supporting the request, the offence:

item.p: is punishable by deprivation of liberty for a maximum period of at least one year or a more severe sentence both under the law of Switzerland and under the law of the requesting State and
is not subject to Swiss jurisdiction.

blockList.listIntroduction: In determining whether an act is an offence under Swiss law, the following are not considered:

item.p: its specific degrees of guilt and conditions for criminal liability;

the conditions relating to the personal and time-related application of the Swiss Criminal Code
SR 311.0 and the Swiss Military Criminal Code of 13 June 1927
SR 321.0 with regard to the criminal provisions on genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes.
Amended by No I 4 of the FA of 18 June 2010 on the Amendment of the Federal Act in Implementation of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2010 4963; BBl 2008 3863).

content.p: As an exception, the defendant may be extradited for an offence which comes under Swiss jurisdiction if special circumstances, especially the possibility of better social rehabilitation, justify it.
If one of two or more offences is extraditable (Art. 35 para. 1), extradition may be granted for all offences.

Extradition may be denied if Switzerland can assume responsibility for the prosecution of the offence or the execution of the foreign criminal judgment and if this appears to be appropriate with regard to the social rehabilitation of the defendant.

Extradition shall be denied if the request is based on a verdict issued in the absence of the defendant and if the minimum rights of the defence to which a defendant is recognised to be entitled were not respected in the proceedings preceding the verdict; this rule does not apply if the requesting State gives sufficient assurances to guarantee the defendant the right to new court proceedings where the rights of the defence are respected.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

Extradition shall also be denied if the requesting State fails to guarantee that the defendant will not be sentenced to death, that an already pronounced death penalty will not be carried out, or that he will not be subjected to treatment that will impair his physical integrity.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The defendant may be extradited only on condition that the requesting State:

item.p: neither prosecutes nor sentences nor re-extradites him to a third State for any offence committed prior to his extradition and for which extradition was not granted;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).
item.p: does not deprive him of his liberty on any other ground that existed before his extradition;

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).
item.p: does not bring him before an extraordinary court; and moreover
sends the Swiss authorities, at their request, an officially certified copy of the decision which concludes the criminal proceedings.

blockList.listIntroduction: The conditions of paragraph 1 letters a and b no longer apply if:

item.p: the defendant or extradited expressly waives them; or

blockList.listIntroduction: the person extradited:

item.p: in spite of being advised of the consequences has not left the territory of the requesting State within forty-five days of his conditional or final release despite having the opportunity to do so, or if, after leaving that territory, he has returned, or

has been returned by a third State.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: If the extradited person is charged with other offences, the State to which he was extradited may be permitted, on making a new request, to prosecute these offences as well.

article.heading: Requests by more than one State

content.p: If two or more States request extradition for the same offence, extradition shall be granted as a rule to the State where the offence was committed or principally perpetrated.

If extradition is requested by more than one State for different offences, the decision shall be made having due regard to all circumstances, especially the seriousness of the offences, the place of commission, the chronological order in which the requests were received, the nationality of the defendant, the better prospect of social rehabilitation and the possibility of extradition to another State.

In addition to the documents specified in Article 28 paragraph 3, the following shall be enclosed with the request: the original or an officially authenticated copy of an enforceable judgment, of an arrest warrant or of any other document issued in accordance with the regulations of the requesting State and having the same effect.

blockList.listIntroduction: Requests for tracing and arrest with a view to extradition shall contain, in addition to the items of information specified in Article 28 paragraphs 2 and 3 letter a, references to the following:

item.p: the existence of a valid arrest warrant, its date of issue and the name of the issuing authority;
the intention of the competent authority to make a request for extradition.

content.p: The FOJ shall decide whether and under what conditions it will consider the request.

Foreign nationals may be arrested with a view to extradition on the basis of a request by an Interpol National Central Bureau or the Ministry of Justice of another State or on the basis of an international alert in a police search system.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1). Article 52 paragraphs 1 and 2 apply by analogy.
At the time of arrest, objects and assets which can serve as evidence in foreign criminal proceedings or which originate from an offence shall be seized.
The cantonal authorities may, if necessary, order that the arrested person or the rooms be searched.

article.heading: Notice of execution. Duration of measures

content.p: Arrest and seizure shall be reported to the FOJ.
They shall continue until a decision concerning the detention awaiting extradition is issued but at the latest until the third workday after the arrest.

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOJ shall issue an arrest warrant with a view to extradition. It may decline to do so, especially if the defendant:

item.p: will probably not elude extradition and will not endanger the criminal investigation; or
can prove without delay that he was not at the place of the offence when it was committed.

content.p: If the defendant is unfit to remain in detention or if there are other valid reasons, the FOJ may order measures other than detention to ensure his presence.
At the same time the FOJ shall rule on which objects and assets will remain seized or must be seized.

blockList.listIntroduction: Rulings under Article 47 shall contain:

item.p: information, provided by the foreign authority, concerning the identity of the defendant and the offence alleged against this person;
the name of the office which made the request;
the confirmation that extradition will be requested;
the notice regarding the right of appeal under paragraph 2 and the right to appoint a legal adviser.

content.p:
An appeal against these rulings may be filed with the Appeals Chamber of the Federal Criminal Court within ten days of the serving of the written arrest warrant with a view to extradition. Articles 379–397 CrimPC
SR 312.0 apply by analogy to the appeal procedure.
Amended by Annex 1 No II 13 of the Criminal Procedure Code of 5 Oct. 2007, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2010 1881; BBl 2006 1085).
The execution of rulings under Article 47 is a matter for the cantonal authorities.

The arrest warrant with a view to extradition may not be executed while the defendant is held in detention awaiting trial or is serving a sentence.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).
The defendant may neither be released nor deported from Switzerland without the consent of the FOJ.

The FOJ shall order the release of the person concerned from detention 18 days after arrest if the request for extradition and the documents supporting it have not been received.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1). This period may be extended for special cause by up to 40 days.
If the defendant is already detained, the period shall start when he is detained with a view to extradition.

By way of exception, the person concerned may be released from detention with a view to extradition at any stage of the proceedings if this is appropriate in the circumstances. The defendant may lodge a petition for release at any time.

In addition, Articles 238–240 CrimPC
SR 312.0 apply by analogy to release from detention.
Amended by Annex 1 No II 13 of the Criminal Procedure Code of 5 Oct. 2007, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2010 1881; BBl 2006 1085).
If the request and its enclosures are received in time and if extradition is not obviously inadmissible, detention shall continue throughout the proceedings without special ruling.
If the defendant has been released, detention with a view to extradition may be ordered again.

The request and the documents supporting it shall be submitted to the defendant and to his legal adviser. When formally presenting the defendant with the arrest warrant with a view to extradition, the cantonal authority shall ascertain if the defendant is identical with the person mentioned in the request. It shall explain to him the conditions of extradition and of simplified extradition and advise him of the right to appeal, to appoint a legal adviser or to have a legal adviser officially appointed.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

The defendant shall be questioned briefly about his personal circumstances, and especially his nationality and relationship with the requesting State, and asked if and for what reasons he raises objections to the arrest warrant or his extradition. His legal adviser may assist in this hearing.

If the extradited person is to be prosecuted for other offences or re-extradited to a third State, the FOJ shall arrange for him to be questioned on the record in accordance with paragraph 2 by a judicial authority of the requesting State.
If the defendant claims to be able to prove that he was not at the scene of the offence when it was committed, the FOJ shall make the necessary investigations.

Extradition shall be denied in clear cases. In other cases, the exculpatory evidence shall be submitted to the requesting State which shall be asked to declare within a short time whether it wishes to continue with its request.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: If the defendant places on the record before a judicial authority that he waives the requirement of extradition proceedings, the FOJ shall order his surrender unless there are special considerations prohibiting it.
This waiver may be revoked provided the FOJ has not ordered the surrender.
Simplified extradition shall have the effect of extradition and is subject to the same conditions. The requesting State shall be given notice thereof.

After setting the defendant and the third party objecting to the handing over of objects an appropriate deadline for stating their position, the FOJ shall rule on the extradition of the defendant and the handing over of objects and assets seized.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

If the defendant claims that he is being charged with a political offence or if the investigation reveals serious grounds to believe that the offence is of a political nature, the Appeals Chamber of the Federal Criminal Court shall decide the case.
Amended by Annex No 30 of the FA of 17 June 2005 on the Federal Administrative Court, in force since 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202). The FOJ shall send the file to this Court, together with its proposal. The defendant shall be given the opportunity to state his position.

The procedure for an appeal under Article 25 applies by analogy.
Amended by Annex No 30 of the Federal Act of 17 June 2005 on the Federal Administrative Court, in force since 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I 3 of the FA of 1 Oct. 2010 on the Coordination of Asylum and Extradition Procedures, in force since 1 April 2011 (AS 2011 925; BBl 2010 1467).

content.p:
If the defendant has applied for asylum under the Asylum Act of 26 June 1998
SR 142.31, the FOJ and the appellate authority shall consult the files from the asylum proceedings when deciding on extradition.

blockList.listIntroduction: Extradition may be executed if the defendant:

item.p: expressly requests his own immediate extradition; or
does not give notice within five days of the issue of the ruling that he will file an appeal.

content.p: If extradition is refused, the FOJ shall release the person concerned from detention with a view to extradition.
The FOJ shall issue the necessary rulings in agreement with the cantonal authorities.
It shall notify the requesting State of the decision as well as of the date and place of extradition.
Extradition may be postponed provided the person to be extradited is being prosecuted in Switzerland for other offences or if he has to serve a sentence involving deprivation of liberty.

blockList.listIntroduction: However, provisional surrender of the defendant may be granted if:

item.p: this will not be prejudicial to the Swiss criminal proceedings; and
the requesting State has guaranteed to keep the defendant in custody during his stay in that State and will return him regardless of his nationality.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

article.heading: Handing over of objects and assets

blockList.listIntroduction: If the conditions set for the extradition are met, objects and assets shall also be handed over which:

item.p: can serve as evidence; or
derive from the offence.

content.p: If an authority, or a third party with rights acquired in good faith, or the victim who lives in Switzerland asserts rights over the objects or assets which can serve as evidence, their handing over shall be subject to the condition that the requesting State guarantees their return without costs after the conclusion of its proceedings.

blockList.listIntroduction: The objects or assets which derive from the offence include:

item.p: instruments which served to commit the offence;
products or profits of the offence, their replacement value and any unlawful advantage;
gifts and other benefits which served to instigate the offence or recompense the perpetrator for the offence, as well as their replacement value.

blockList.listIntroduction: The objects or assets which derive from the offence may be retained in Switzerland if:

item.p: the victim is habitually resident in Switzerland and they have to be returned to him;
an authority asserts rights over them; or

a person not involved in the offence and whose claims are not guaranteed by the requesting State shows probable cause that he has acquired rights over the objects and assets in good faith in Switzerland, or, if he is habitually resident in Switzerland, in a foreign country.

content.p: Objects or assets mentioned in the first paragraph and which are required for pending criminal proceedings in Switzerland may also be retained in Switzerland.

blockList.listIntroduction: If a person entitled to the objects or assets makes a claim under paragraph 4, the objects or assets shall not be handed over until the legal position has been clarified. Objects or assets in dispute shall be returned to the person entitled only if:

item.p: the requesting State gives its consent;
in the case of paragraph 4 letter b, the authority gives its consent; or
the justification of the claim is recognised by a Swiss judicial authority.

content.p: The handing over of objects and assets is not dependent on the execution of the extradition of the defendant.

Objects and assets in accordance with paragraph 1 letter b to which Switzerland is entitled according to an asset-sharing agreement based on the Federal Act of 19 March 2004
SR 312.4 on the Division of Forfeited Assets are not handed over.
Inserted by Annex No 2 of the FA of 19 March 2004 on the Division of Forfeited Assets, in force since 1 August 2004 (AS 2004 3503; BBl 2002 441).

If objects or assets are handed over and their return is waived, the customs lien or any other real liability under Swiss customs or tax law shall not be claimed if the owner who suffered loss as a result of the offence does not personally owe the duty or tax.
The waiver of such a fiscal lien may be made dependent on reciprocity.

If the requesting State does not take the necessary steps to take over the person to be extradited within ten days of notification of the execution order, he shall be released. This time limit may be extended up to 30 days in response to a justified request from the requesting State.

In the event of extradition to a foreign country, the Swiss Confederation shall pay the costs of detention and transportation provided that it is customary in international relations for the requested State to pay such costs.
The personal property of the defendant may be used to cover the costs provided it does not have to be handed over to the requesting State.

Mutual assistance within the meaning of Part Three of this Act shall comprise the transmission of information, as well as procedural acts and other official acts permitted under Swiss law provided these acts appear to be necessary for proceedings carried out abroad in criminal matters or serve to retrieve the proceeds of the offence.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: Mutual assistance measures shall include in particular:

item.p: the service of documents;
obtaining evidence, and in particular searching persons and rooms, seizure, orders to produce, expert opinions, conducting hearings and confrontations of persons;
production of documents and papers;

handing over of objects or assets with a view to forfeiture or for restitution to the entitled person.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: The following shall, in particular, be considered proceedings carried out in criminal matters:

item.p: prosecution of criminal offences as provided for in Article 1 paragraph 3;
administrative measures against an offender;
execution of criminal judgments and pardons;

compensation for unjustified detention.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: Assistance may also be granted to the European Court of Human Rights and to the European Commission on Human Rights in proceedings regarding the safeguarding of human rights and fundamental freedoms.
Assistance which will exonerate a defendant is permitted even if the request is inadmissible under Articles 3–5.

Measures under Article 63 which require the use of procedural compulsion may be ordered only if the description of the circumstances of the case indicates that the offence being prosecuted abroad contains the objective elements of an offence under Swiss law. The measures must be carried out in accordance with Swiss law.

blockList.listIntroduction: If the offence prosecuted abroad is not an offence in Switzerland, measures under Article 63 which require the use of procedural compulsion shall be allowed for:

item.p: the exoneration of a defendant;

item.num:
b.
Amended by Annex No 16 of the FA of 19 Dec. 2008 (Adult Protection, Law of Persons and Law of Children), in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2011 725; BBl 2006 7001).
item.p:
the prosecution of offences involving sexual acts with minors.
Amended by Annex No 4 of the FA of 13 Dec. 2002, in force since 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 3459; BBl 1999 1979).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: At the express request of the foreign State:

item.p: the statements of witnesses or experts shall be affirmed in the form prescribed by the laws of the requesting State, even if the applicable Swiss law does not provide such a form;
forms necessary to obtain other evidence that is admissible in court may be taken into consideration.

content.p: Forms for obtaining and affirming evidence according to paragraph 1 must be compatible with Swiss law, and no essential prejudice may result therefrom to the persons involved.

A person may also refuse to testify provided the law of the requesting State so provides or if the fact of testifying may cause criminal or disciplinary sanctions to be imposed under the laws of that State or of the State where the examined person lives.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

article.heading: Presence of persons participating in proceedings abroad

content.p: When the requesting State, based on its law, so requests, persons who are participating in proceedings abroad may be authorised to attend mutual assistance proceedings and to have access to the files.
Their presence may also be permitted if it substantially helps to facilitate the execution of the request or the foreign criminal proceedings.
Their presence may not lead to their obtaining access to information within the scope of secrecy before the appropriate authority has decided whether, and to what extent, assistance may be granted.

article.heading:
Principle of «Ne bis in idem»
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: Assistance may be denied if the defendant resides in Switzerland and proceedings are already pending here regarding the offence to which the request relates.

However, assistance may be granted if the proceedings carried out abroad are not directed solely against the defendant who is residing in Switzerland, or if the execution of the request serves to exonerate him.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: Information and documents obtained through mutual assistance may not be used for investigative purposes or as evidence in the requesting State in any proceedings relating to an offence for which assistance is not admissible.

blockList.listIntroduction: Any further use shall be subject to approval by the FOJ. This approval is not necessary if:

item.p: the act to which the request relates constitutes another offence for which mutual assistance would be granted; or
the foreign criminal proceedings are directed against other persons who have participated in committing the offence.

content.p: Presence at the mutual assistance proceedings and access to the files shall be permitted under the same conditions (Art. 65a para.1).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

article.heading: Spontaneous transmission of information and evidence

blockList.listIntroduction: An authority prosecuting offences may, without being requested to do so, transmit to a foreign authority prosecuting offences information or evidence that it has gathered in the course of its own investigation, when it determines that this transmission may:

item.p: permit the opening of criminal proceedings; or
facilitate an ongoing criminal investigation.

content.p: The transmission as defined in paragraph 1 does not have any effect on the criminal proceedings pending in Switzerland.
The transmission of evidence to a State with which Switzerland does not have an international agreement shall be subject to authorisation by the FOJ.
Paragraphs 1 and 2 do not apply to evidence that is subject to the rules on secrecy.
Information that is subject to the rules on secrecy may be transmitted if it may enable the foreign State to present a request for mutual assistance.
A record shall be made of each spontaneous transmission.
Where a Swiss authority is requested to serve documents, service may be effected by personal or postal delivery to the recipient.
The Federal Council may permit the direct service of documents from abroad to the recipient in Switzerland. It shall determine the conditions for such service.
Service is presumed to be effected if acceptance or refusal to accept has been confirmed in writing.
There is no obligation to comply for any person who accepts a summons to appear before a foreign authority.
Summonses containing threats of compulsion shall not be served.

Service of a summons may be made subject to the condition that the recipient is guaranteed safe conduct for an appropriate period of time and will not be prevented from freely leaving the territory of the requesting State. If the recipient so requires, the authority effecting service shall ask the requesting State to give a written assurance thereof before proof of service is furnished.

Persons held in custody in Switzerland may be transferred to a foreign authority for the purpose of investigations if they are guaranteed safe conduct and if it is guaranteed that they will be kept in custody and returned to Switzerland on request.

Persons who are not indicted abroad and Swiss citizens may be transferred only with their written consent. This is not necessary if the transfer is required for the execution of a Swiss request or for confrontation with other persons abroad.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, with effect from 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: If a detained person is surrendered to the Swiss authorities in the course of an act of assistance, the warrant for his arrest issued abroad shall also be valid in Switzerland for the period of his stay in Switzerland.
During transit the defendant shall be kept in custody by virtue of the order for transit given by the FOJ.
In those cases the detained person may be released only with the agreement of the competent foreign authority.

A person habitually resident abroad and who appears in Switzerland in a criminal case pursuant to a summons may neither be prosecuted nor restricted in his personal freedom for reasons that occurred prior to his entry into Switzerland.
The defendant shall enjoy no safe conduct regarding the offences specified in the summons.
The safe conduct provided for in paragraph 1 shall cease when this person leaves Switzerland but at the latest three days after he is permitted to leave by the summoning authorities.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: On request, objects, documents or assets seized as evidence as well as records and decisions shall be made available to the competent foreign authority after conclusion of the mutual assistance proceedings (Art. 80d).

If a third party with rights acquired in good faith, an authority, or the victim who is habitually resident in Switzerland claim that they have rights over the objects, documents or assets under paragraph 1, their handing over shall be subject to the condition that the requesting State gives the guarantee to return them free of charge after the conclusion of the proceedings.
Return may be delayed if the objects, documents or assets are necessary for criminal proceedings pending in Switzerland.
Article 60 applies to fiscal liens.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

article.heading: Handing over of objects or assets for the purpose of forfeiture or return

content.p: On request, objects or assets subject to a precautionary seizure may be handed over to the competent foreign authority after conclusion of the mutual assistance proceedings (Art. 80d) for the purpose of forfeiture or return to the person entitled.

blockList.listIntroduction: The objects or assets referred to in paragraph 1 include:

item.p: instruments which were used to commit the offence;
products of or profits from the offence, their replacement value and any unlawful advantage;
gifts and other contributions which served to instigate the offence or recompense the offender, as well as their replacement value.

content.p: The handing over may take place at any stage of the foreign proceedings, normally based on a final and executable decision from the requesting State.

blockList.listIntroduction: However, the objects or assets may be retained in Switzerland if:

item.p: the victim is habitually resident in Switzerland and they have to be returned to him;
an authority asserts rights over them;

a person not involved in the offence and whose claims are not guaranteed by the requesting State shows probable cause that he has acquired rights over these objects and assets in good faith in Switzerland, or if he is habitually resident in Switzerland, in a foreign country; or
the objects or assets are necessary for pending criminal proceedings in Switzerland or appear, because of their nature, to be subject to forfeiture in Switzerland.

blockList.listIntroduction: Whenever a person claims to have rights over the objects or assets under paragraph 4, its handing over to the requesting State shall be postponed until the legal situation is clear. The objects or assets claimed may be handed over to the person entitled if:

item.p: the requesting State agrees;
in the case of paragraph 4 letter b, the authority gives its consent; or
the claim has been recognised by a Swiss court.

content.p: Article 60 applies to fiscal liens.

Objects and assets to which Switzerland is entitled according to an asset sharing agreement based on the Federal Act of 19 March 2004
SR 312.4 on the Division of Forfeited Assets shall not be handed over in accordance with paragraph 1.
Inserted by Annex No 2 of the FA of 19 March 2004 on the Division of Forfeited Assets, in force since 1 August 2004 (AS 2004 3503; BBl 2002 441).
Requests for assistance may be submitted by authorities that are competent to investigate offences or make decisions in other proceedings to which this Act is applicable.

Swiss authorities may also accept requests for the execution of procedural acts from the parties authorised to make them if those acts are incumbent upon the parties under the laws of the requesting State.

The FOJ shall make requests for mutual assistance that is needed outside criminal proceedings.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

content.p: The commissioners of police of the Confederation and of the cantons may make a request under Article 63 on their own behalf and may grant such requests emanating from foreign authorities.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following requests are excluded:

item.p: requests which necessitate the use of procedural compulsion;
requests for information or measures in proceedings regarding extradition, transfer of proceedings and execution of criminal judgments;
requests for the handing over of criminal decisions or criminal files.

blockList.listIntroduction: In addition to the information and documents required by Article 28, the following shall be specified in or enclosed with a request:

item.p: in requests for service: the name and address of the recipient and his position in the proceedings as well as the type of document to be served;
with requests for transit: one of the documents listed in Article 41;
with requests for search of persons or rooms, for seizure or handing over of objects: confirmation that these measures are permitted in the requesting State.

Section 2

section.heading: Treatment of the Request

content.p: The FOJ shall receive foreign requests unless provision is made for direct transmission to the competent cantonal or federal executing authority.

The FOJ shall summarily examine whether the request meets the formal requirements of this Act and shall forward it to the appropriate executing authority unless the request clearly appears to be inadmissible.
If necessary, the FOJ shall return the request to the requesting State for improvement or completion.
Receipt and transmission of the request to the competent authority are not subject to appeal.
The procedural provisions of Article 18 are reserved.

If the execution of the request necessitates investigations in more than one canton or if it also concerns a federal authority, the FOJ may entrust a single authority with its execution. Articles 44–47, 52 and 53 CrimPC
SR 312.0 apply by analogy.
Second sentence Amended by Annex 1 No II 13 of the Criminal Procedure Code of 5 Oct. 2007, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2010 1881; BBl 2006 1085).
The FOJ may delegate all or part of the execution of a request to the federal authority which would be competent if the offence had been committed in Switzerland.
The FOJ may also entrust the execution of supplementary requests to the authority to which execution was delegated.
The designation of the cantonal or federal authority responsible shall not be subject to appeal.

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOJ may decide whether mutual assistance is permitted and delegate its execution to a cantonal authority or itself decide on the execution if:

item.p: the execution of the request necessitates investigations in more than one canton;
the competent cantonal authority is unable to make a decision within the appropriate time; or
the cases are complex or particularly important.

content.p: The request shall be subject to preliminary examination by the cantonal or federal authority responsible for its execution.
If the request cannot be granted, the executing authority shall return it to the requesting authority by the same channel through which it was received.
The executing authority shall issue a summary ruling on whether to consider the case and shall order the mutual assistance measures permitted.
It shall execute the mutual assistance measures in accordance with its own procedural law.

article.heading: Participation in the proceedings and access to the files

content.p: The persons entitled may participate in the proceedings and have access to the files provided this is necessary to safeguard their interests.

blockList.listIntroduction: The rights provided for in paragraph 1 may be limited only:

item.p: in the interest of the foreign proceedings;
for the protection of an important legal interest if the requesting State so requests;
because of the nature or urgency of the measures to be taken;
for the protection of important private interests;
in the interest of Swiss proceedings.

content.p: Access to the files or participation in the proceedings may only be denied in the case of files or procedural measures for reasons of confidentiality.

The persons entitled, and in particular the holders of documents, information or assets may consent to handing them over without formality at any time prior to the conclusion of the proceedings. Consent is irrevocable.
If all the persons entitled give their consent, the competent authority shall make a written record thereof and conclude the proceedings.
If only some of the documents, information or assets required are handed over, the ordinary proceedings shall be followed for the remaining part.

article.heading: Conclusion of the mutual assistance proceedings

content.p: When the executing authority determines that the request is completely or partially executed, it shall issue a ruling giving reasons on whether mutual assistance is granted and to what extent.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex No II 5 of the FedD of 25 Sept. 2020 on the Approval and Implementation of the Council of Europe Convention on the Prevention of Terrorism and its Additional Protocol and the Strengthening of Criminal Justice Instruments for combating Terrorism and Organised Crime, in force since 1 July 2021 (AS 2021 360; BBl 2018 6427).

article.heading: Early transmission of information and evidence

blockList.listIntroduction: The competent cantonal or federal authority may by way of exception order the early transmission of information or evidence gathered before the final ruling is issued:

item.p: if foreign investigations in cases relating to organised crime or terrorism would be made disproportionately difficult without this mutual assistance measure, in particular where there is a risk of collusion or in order to safeguard the confidentiality of the proceedings; or
in order to avert a serious and immediate danger, and in particular the commission of a terrorist offence.

content.p: The information or evidence concerned must be connected with the prevention or the prosecution of an extraditable criminal offence.

Early transmission may be ordered with or without a request being received. If it is ordered in the absence of a request, the competent cantonal or federal authority shall transmit only the non-personal data required to assess the position, subject to receiving the undertakings specified in paragraph 4.

blockList.listIntroduction: Early transmission is conditional on the requesting authority providing an undertaking in advance that:

item.p: the information or evidence will be used solely to assist with investigations, and under no circumstances for the purpose of requesting, justifying or issuing a final decision;

it will inform the competent cantonal or federal authority as soon as the foreign proceedings permit that the person concerned may be notified of the early transmission under Article 80m so that he or she can respond before the final ruling is issued;
it will remove the information or evidence obtained through early transmission from the files for the foreign proceedings if mutual assistance is refused.

content.p: Notification of the person concerned shall be deferred.
Notice of the interim ruling in accordance with paragraph 1 shall be given to the FOJ without delay and before the early transmission. It is not in itself contestable.

section.heading: Joint Investigation Team

article.heading: Appointment of a joint investigation team

content.p: The cantonal or federal mutual assistance authority may for a specific purpose and in consultation with the competent foreign judicial authority appoint a joint investigation team (JIT) to conduct or support the conduct of a criminal investigation in a state participating in the JIT.

A JIT may in particular be appointed in a difficult or complex criminal investigation that involves one or more other states and which requires considerable resources as well as coordinated and concerted action.
It may only be appointed if a request for mutual assistance has been submitted by a judicial authority.
The JIT must be appointed for a limited duration. The appointment may be extended as required.
The competent authority shall designate the persons responsible and the members of the JIT for its state. The JIT may call on the services of experts and auxiliary personnel as required.
Notice of the act of appointment shall be given to the FOJ in writing.
The JIT’s activities are governed by the law of the state in which the investigation is conducted.
The representative of the criminal or mutual assistance authority in whose state an investigative measure is carried out is responsible for that investigative measure.

article.heading: Status in relation to criminal and civil liability

content.p: The foreign person responsible and the foreign members of the JIT, as well as the foreign experts and auxiliary personnel under Article 80dter paragraph 5 are deemed equivalent to the Swiss person responsible and the Swiss members of the JIT during an operation on Swiss national territory in relation to any offences committed against them or that they themselves commit. They are also deemed equivalent to them in relation to any injury, loss or damage that they cause during their operation.

article.heading: Access to documents, information and evidence

blockList.listIntroduction: The persons responsible and members of the JIT shall have access to:

item.p: documents and information that are related to the relevant criminal investigation;
evidence that has been gathered in the course of the relevant criminal investigation.

content.p: They shall be denied access to documents, information and evidence if a decision to that effect has been taken by a person responsible for the JIT or by a criminal or mutual assistance authority. The foregoing also applies if the documents, information or evidence were obtained before the JIT was appointed.
The experts and auxiliary personnel under Article 80dter paragraph 5 shall have access only to documents, information and evidence that are required for them to fulfil the tasks assigned to them.
The early transmission of documents, information and evidence that are to located on Swiss sovereign territory is governed by Article 80dbis.
The confidentiality of the information, including the confidentiality of the investigation, must be preserved.
The protection of personal data is governed by the law of the state in which the investigative measure is carried out.

If the bodies normally competent to do so in the judicial authorities concerned intend to issue a press release, the Swiss criminal or mutual assistance authority and its foreign partner authority shall discuss the content beforehand.
The costs of the investigative activities shall be borne by the state in which the act concerned is carried out.
The costs related to time spent in the other country, travel and accommodation for the persons responsible and the other members of the JIT shall be borne by their own country.

The rooms and the technical resources required to conduct the investigative activities, such as office space, communication media or special equipment, shall be provided by the state in which the activity concerned is carried out.

blockList.listIntroduction: The act of appointment must include the following information:

item.p: the purpose of the JIT;
the names of the Swiss and the foreign criminal or mutual assistance authorities;
the names of the persons responsible for each state participating in the JIT and the names of the other members of the JIT and their functions;
the criminal investigation, including the factual circumstances, that is the subject matter of the criminal investigation, and the offences under investigation;
the states on whose territory the JIT will conduct investigations in accordance with the relevant national law;
the duration for which the JIT is appointed, with the date on which this period ends;

the names of any experts and auxiliary personnel who are not members of the JIT, in particular of those who come from other services or administrative units in the participating states, as well as the names of any experts and auxiliary personnel from Eurojust and Europol;
the procedure for dealings with the media;
the arrangements for bearing the costs of the criminal investigation and investigative activities;
the arrangements for bearing the costs of time spent in the other country, travel and accommodation for the persons responsible, the other members of the JIT and the experts and auxiliary personnel;
the technical resources required to conduct the operations.

content.p: The act of appointment may be amended if the investigations so require. In particular, further members may be added to the JIT or the time limit may be extended.

the presence of persons involved in the foreign proceedings.

section.heading: Special Provisions

blockList.listIntroduction: The executing authority and the appellate authority shall give notice of their rulings to:

item.p: the entitled person living in Switzerland;
the entitled person living abroad and with an address for service of documents in Switzerland.

content.p: The right to notification shall end when the ruling concluding the mutual assistance proceedings becomes legally enforceable.

Holders of documents have the right to inform their clients of the existence of the request and of all the facts relating thereto unless the competent authority has, as an exception, expressly prohibited this and made reference to Article 292 of the Swiss Criminal Code
SR 311.0 and the penalties that it carries.
The person entitled who intervenes in pending proceedings may no longer challenge rulings that have become legally enforceable.

article.heading: Inquiry addressed to the requesting State

content.p: If additional information is necessary, the executing or the appellate authority shall request the FOJ to obtain it from the requesting State.
If necessary, the competent authority shall suspend dealing with all or part of the request and rule on the points that may be dealt with based on the documents available.

The FOJ shall give the requesting State an appropriate deadline by which to respond. If the deadline given is not respected, the request for mutual assistance shall be examined based on the documents available.
The executing and the appellate authority as well as the FOJ may make the granting of mutual assistance wholly or partly subject to certain conditions.

The FOJ shall communicate the conditions to the requesting State when the ruling on the granting and the extent of the mutual assistance is final and shall give it an appropriate deadline by which to accept or refuse. If the deadline given is not respected, mutual assistance may be granted on the points that are not subject to conditions.
The FOJ shall examine if the response of the requesting State satisfies the conditions set.

The ruling of the FOJ is subject to an appeal to the Appeals Chamber of the Federal Criminal Court within ten days of its notice being given in writing. The decision of the Appeals Chamber is final.
Amended by Annex No 30 of the FA of 17 June 2005 on the Federal Administrative Court, in force since 1 Jan. 2007 (AS 2006 2197; BBl 2001 4202).

blockList.listIntroduction: The requesting State shall be charged for:

item.p: the remuneration of experts;
the return of objects or assets for the purpose of restitution to the person entitled.
