section.heading: Prosecution in Switzerland on behalf of another State

blockList.listIntroduction: At the request of the State in which the offence was committed, Switzerland may prosecute on its behalf an offence committed abroad if:

item.p: extradition is not permitted;
the defendant has to face charges in Switzerland for other more serious offences; and
it is guaranteed that the requesting State will not prosecute him for the same offence after acquittal or completing a sentence in Switzerland.

content.p: A foreign national who is habitually resident in Switzerland may also be prosecuted in Switzerland if his extradition cannot be justified and prosecution in Switzerland seems appropriate with regard to his personal situation and social rehabilitation.

These provisions do not apply if the offence is subject to Swiss jurisdiction on the basis of another provision.
Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).
The offence shall be judged according to Swiss law as if it had been committed in Switzerland.
The foreign law applies if it is more lenient. The court may impose only the sentences provided for by Swiss law.
Proceedings in the absence of the defendant are not permitted.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex 1 No II 13 of the Criminal Procedure Code of 5 Oct. 2007, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2010 1881; BBl 2006 1085).

content.p:
If Swiss jurisdiction is not yet established, it shall be determined in accordance with Article 32 CrimPC
SR 312.0.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, in force since 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

blockList.listIntroduction: Another State may be requested to prosecute an offence subject to Swiss jurisdiction if its laws allow the prosecution and judicial punishment of the offence and if:

item.p: the defendant is present there and his extradition to Switzerland is inappropriate or not permitted; or
he is extradited to this State and the transfer of the prosecution offers the prospect of better social rehabilitation.

blockList.listIntroduction: If another State prosecutes the offence, the Swiss authorities may not take further measures against the defendant for the same offence:

item.p: unless the requested State has given notice that it is not in a position to conclude the prosecution; or
if, according to the decision made in the requested State, the conditions of Article 5 letter a or b are met.

content.p:
The effect of the time limitation provisions under Swiss law is suspended provided the proceedings including enforcement of the sentence are ongoing in the requested State.
The suspension of the effects of the time limitation provisions has been abolished by Art. 97 ff. of the Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) and time limits for execution have been replaced by an extension of the regular time limit (AS 2006 3459; BBl 1999 1979).

If the defendant was extradited to the requested State for other offences, this State need not observe the conditions of extradition in accordance with Article 38 provided it grants the request for prosecution.
In addition to the documents specified in Article 28 paragraph 3, the record of criminal proceedings as well as any evidentiary productions must be enclosed with the request.
The FOJ shall decide on whether to accept the foreign request after consulting the prosecuting authorities.
If it accepts the request, it shall transmit the file to the prosecuting authority and notify the requesting State and the person concerned.
The decision does not create an obligation to institute criminal proceedings.
The FOJ may refuse to assume responsibility for the prosecution if there is good cause not to do so or if the seriousness of the offence does not justify it.
Any investigative measure carried out by the authorities of the requesting State under its law shall be considered equivalent to a corresponding Swiss investigative measure.
The costs of the proceedings set by the requesting State shall be added to the costs of the proceedings in Switzerland and collected. They are not refunded to the requesting State.

The cantons shall have a right of disposal over any fines paid and, subject to the provisions of the Federal Act of 19 March 2004
SR 312.4 on the Division of Forfeited Assets, over forfeited objects.
Amended by Annex No 2 of the FA of 19 March 2004 on the Division of Forfeited Assets, in force since 1 August 2004 (AS 2004 3503; BBl 2002 441).
The requested State shall be notified of the costs of the proceedings incurred in Switzerland if the requested State takes over the prosecution. Their reimbursement shall not be requested.

blockList.listIntroduction: Final and enforceable criminal judgments from another State may be enforced at that State's request if:

item.p: the convicted person is habitually resident in Switzerland or has to face charges here for a serious offence;
the subject of the conviction is an offence committed abroad which, if committed in Switzerland, would be punishable here; and
enforcement in Switzerland seems to be appropriate for one of the reasons specified in Article 85 paragraphs 1 and 2 or likely to be barred in the requesting State.

content.p: Sentences imposed abroad shall be executed provided they do not exceed the maximum penalty provided by Swiss law for a corresponding offence. Sentences that remain below the minimum penalty according to Swiss law may be executed.

…
Repealed by No I of the FA of 4 Oct. 1996, with effect from 1 Feb. 1997 (AS 1997 114; BBl 1995 III 1).

Fines as well as costs arising from proceedings under Article 63 may also be enforced if the convicted person is habitually resident abroad but has assets at his disposal in Switzerland and if the requesting State grants reciprocity.

blockList.listIntroduction: The order permitting enforcement (exequatur) may not be issued if:

item.num:
a.
The amendment in accordance with Art. 97 ff. of the Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) contains a limitation system (AS 2006 3459; BBl 1999 1979).
item.p: the conviction took place at a time when, under Swiss law, the prosecution would have been time barred;
the sentence would have been time barred under Swiss law if a Swiss authority had imposed it at the same time; or
the offence is also subject to Swiss jurisdiction and no sentence could be imposed under Swiss law for other reasons.

content.p: Decisions on costs shall be declared enforceable only if the costs are to be paid to the State.

blockList.listIntroduction: The court shall refuse to enforce in whole or in part if:

item.p: the convicted person has incurred a sentence involving deprivation of liberty in Switzerland for other offences and enforcement as requested would result in an obviously more severe punishment than if the offences taken as a whole were judged in Switzerland; or
the execution of any of the accessory criminal measures in Switzerland is not permitted, or

it is of the opinion that the convicted person has good reason to oppose the enforcement of a judgment or penalty order that was issued in his absence and which is no longer subject to a right of objection or appeal under the law of the requesting State.

article.heading: Binding force of the findings in fact

content.p: In assessing criminal liability and the possibility of prosecution under Swiss law, the court shall be bound to the findings in fact on which the decision relies. If they do not suffice, the gathering of evidence may be ordered.
If Switzerland assumes responsibility for enforcement, no criminal proceedings against the convicted person for the same offence may be instituted or continued here.

article.heading: Use of Swiss institutions by foreign States

content.p: If the conditions of Article 94 paragraph 1 are not met, sentences involving restriction of liberty that have been imposed on a non-Swiss national in another State may be enforced in Switzerland under Swiss law if the other State cannot execute them itself.
In this case, the final and enforceable foreign decision shall constitute the legal basis for the restriction of the convicted person’s liberty.

If persons are surrendered to Switzerland in accordance with paragraph 1, then unless arrangements to the contrary have been made with the competent authorities of the surrendering State, they may neither be prosecuted nor punished nor extradited to a third State by the Swiss authorities for offences that they committed before their surrender and that were not the subject of their conviction. These effects shall expire ten days after release on parole or final release from the institution.
The Federal Council shall regulate the details.

blockList.listIntroduction: Another State may be requested to enforce a Swiss criminal judgment if:

item.p: it is certain to accept the binding force of the judgment in accordance with Article 97; and
the transfer of enforcement is likely to improve the prospects of the social rehabilitation of the convicted person or if Switzerland cannot obtain his extradition.

content.p: The convicted person who is detained in Switzerland may only be transferred with a view to enforcement of the judgment under Article 100 if he agrees and if the requested State is expected to accept the conditions set by the FOJ.

The convicted person may be transferred without his consent if an international agreement ratified by Switzerland so provides. In this case the conditions and effects of the transfer are regulated exclusively by the said international agreement.
Inserted by art. 2 of the FD of 19 Dec. 2003, in force since 1 Oct. 2004 (AS 2004 4161 4162; BBl 2002 4340).
If another State enforces the criminal judgment, the Swiss authority shall abandon enforcement provided the requested State has not given notice that it will not conclude it.
The convicted person may be taken into custody so as to ensure his transfer.
Article 89 paragraphs 2 and 3 apply by analogy.

blockList.listIntroduction: In addition to the documents specified in Article 28 paragraph 3, the following shall be enclosed with a request:

item.p: the original or an officially authenticated copy of the judgment with a certificate attesting that it is legally enforceable;
a certificate attesting the period of detention undergone in the requesting State;
if the requested State so requests, the original or officially authenticated copy of the criminal file.

content.p: After consulting with the authority which will execute the request, the FOJ shall decide whether to accept the foreign request. If it accepts, it shall convey the file and its opinion to the executing authority and inform the requesting State. Article 91 paragraph 4 applies by analogy.

If there is Swiss jurisdiction and if a sentence which is more severe than the one provided by Swiss law was imposed abroad, the prosecution may be taken over instead of the enforcement of the judgment if the requesting State so requests.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex 1 No II 13 of the Criminal Procedure Code of 5 Oct. 2007, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2010 1881; BBl 2006 1085).

content.p:
The competent court under Article 32 CrimPC
SR 312.0 shall inform the convicted person of the applicable procedure, hear him on the matter, as well as his counsel, and decide on enforcement.
The court shall examine ex officio whether the conditions for enforcement are met and gather the necessary evidence.
If the conditions are met, the court shall declare that the decision may be enforced and take the measures necessary for enforcement.
The decision shall be made in the form of a judgment containing a statement of the rationale therefor. Cantonal law shall provide for an appeal.
The sentence determined by the court shall be executed in accordance with Swiss law.
Execution shall be discontinued if the decision is no longer enforceable in the requesting State.
If enforcement relates solely to a decision on costs, the amounts collected after deduction of the costs incurred shall be transferred to the requesting State if it guarantees reciprocity.
In addition to the costs for the execution of the sentence, the costs of exequatur proceedings and other enforcement measures shall also be regarded as costs in accordance with Article 31.
